sources.title: Proko — Muscle Anatomy of the Hand
sources.kind: Original instructor; publicly readable lesson text
sources.reviewed_access: Public lesson text reviewed; premium downloads not obtained
sources.source_supported_observation: The lesson distinguishes palmar thumb mass, dorsal thumb mass, pinky-side mass, and the changing web relationship.
sources.proposed_application: Shape a substantial thenar pad and a rounded thumb/index web rather than a stretched flat membrane.
sources.limitation: An art-anatomy lesson, not a Blender recipe or a numeric contact standard. Do not redistribute its protected lesson media.

sources.title: Proko — Hands Holding Stuff N Things
sources.reviewed_access: Public description only; full lesson NOT viewed
sources.source_supported_observation: The public description concerns hands holding objects.
sources.proposed_application: Optional further study of enclosure and contact; not a dependency for this task.
sources.limitation: Premium material. No purchase, access, timestamped procedure or full-video analysis is claimed.

sources.title: Blender — Human Base Meshes v1.4.1
sources.reviewed_access: Indexed official listing reviewed; archive NOT downloaded
sources.source_supported_observation: The listing identifies a 49 MB CC0 bundle requiring Blender 4.2 LTS or newer.
sources.proposed_application: An optional alternative editable foundation if the existing derived glove cannot be remodeled efficiently.
sources.limitation: Inspect the actual archive and its component inventory before choosing a hand. This bundle is not a pre-fitted Ada grip.

sources.title: Blender 5.1 — Poly Build
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed; title/interface text partly localized
sources.source_supported_observation: Poly Build combines vertex/face creation, moving and edge extrusion for mesh construction and retopology.
sources.proposed_application: Rebuild the thumb web and reconnect digit roots with explicit faces.
sources.limitation: Use the installed keymap and preview each operation. The tool does not determine anatomy.

sources.title: Blender 5.1 — Bevel Modifier
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: Bevel has selectable edge control, width interpretation, overlap clamping and normal-treatment options.
sources.proposed_application: Author a restrained edge highlight on plate rims without rounding away the entire shape.
sources.limitation: Overlap clamping is not an assembly-level collision solver. A shading fix cannot repair a bad silhouette.

sources.title: Blender 5.1 — Solidify
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed; localized page with English technical passages
sources.source_supported_observation: Thickness is computed in local coordinates; uniform thickness remains an approximation.
sources.proposed_application: Make measured armor shells on new candidates; inspect real section thickness and normals.
sources.limitation: Do not re-enable the known failing even-offset settings on the preserved BW1 garments. No guarantee of collision-free thickness.

sources.title: Blender 5.1 — Apply Pose
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: Pose as Rest Pose changes the armature rest state and affects the skinning relationship.
sources.proposed_application: Avoid changing the shared rig merely to freeze a hand; transform independent geometry into its verified bind space.
sources.limitation: This is not a command to apply the current MPFB pose to the shared game skeleton.

sources.title: Blender — PoseBone matrix semantics
sources.reviewed_access: Matrix semantics reviewed in the documented 4.5 API; local 5.1 API still to verify
sources.source_supported_observation: PoseBone.matrix is the final matrix in armature object space, distinct from matrix_basis.
sources.proposed_application: Include the armature world transform exactly once in hand-local capture and bind-space reconstruction.
sources.limitation: The equations in this kit are a proposed transform contract, not code executed on Ada; verify installed API and actual objects.

sources.title: MPFB — Export Copy
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: Export-copy operations preserve the original character while preparing a derived output hierarchy.
sources.proposed_application: Keep indexed MPFB masters intact and explicitly author a separate fixed-hand output representation.
sources.limitation: Choose operations deliberately; baked subdivision, modifiers and masks can change output geometry. No installed-version test performed here.

sources.title: Epic — Skeletal Mesh Sockets
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: Sockets carry bone-relative attachment offsets; mesh-specific sockets can be used when a shared skeleton needs asset-specific attachments.
sources.proposed_application: Verify the actual sword attachment and isolate any candidate offset instead of editing all characters' shared socket.
sources.limitation: Docs may describe a newer engine than the local project. Do not upgrade or mutate the canonical skeleton implicitly.

sources.title: Epic — FBX Import Options Reference
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: Import settings include skeleton/reference-pose changes and separate normal/tangent policies.
sources.proposed_application: Use an isolated import, preserve reference pose, and verify the selected normal convention.
sources.limitation: An import success is not an art or animation pass; map settings to the actual installed importer.

sources.title: Epic — FBX Skeletal Mesh Pipeline
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: The pipeline supports skeletal meshes/animations and recommends controlling triangulation.
sources.proposed_application: Export a reviewed runtime copy with explicit triangulation and test it on the existing clips.
sources.limitation: The documented FBX 2020.2 pipeline does not imply Blender exports an identical SDK/version; use the already calibrated local profile.

sources.title: The Met — Gauntlet for the Right Hand, 29.158.215
sources.reviewed_access: Collection page and search-returned palm image reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: The record identifies a Milanese steel-and-gold gauntlet; the palm image shows construction unlike the plated dorsal side.
sources.proposed_application: Study separation of the palm covering, finger backing and cuff; keep Ada's palm comparatively simple.
sources.limitation: Do not infer a complete moving mechanism from one still. This is historical structure inspiration, not Ada's final design.

sources.title: The Met — Right Gauntlet, 2002.507
sources.reviewed_access: Collection text and dorsal image reviewed; alternate image endpoints located
sources.source_supported_observation: The listed gauntlet combines steel, textile/leather and rich surface decoration; its image distinguishes cuff, hand plates and finger defenses.
sources.proposed_application: Use the large-to-small plate hierarchy, not its densely ornamented visual treatment.
sources.limitation: The historic object does not validate our closed-hand geometry. Do not reproduce all engraving on Ada.

sources.title: The Met — Locking Gauntlet, 36.149.13
sources.kind: Museum collection; Public Domain image record
sources.reviewed_access: Detailed curator text reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: A specific mitten-type example has articulated metacarpal/finger lames and could be secured closed.
sources.proposed_application: Study overlapping protection and cuff construction. It reinforces the distinction between a designed closed shape and a universal articulated hand.
sources.limitation: Not a requirement to give Ada a mitten or add a locking mechanism; no physical weapon-making guidance intended.

sources.title: The Met — Breastplate, 2014.673
sources.kind: Museum collection; Public Domain image record
sources.reviewed_access: Detailed curator text reviewed; front/back image endpoints located
sources.source_supported_observation: The record describes a main shell, movable armhole gussets, turned edges, shoulder fastening and lower overlapping lames.
sources.proposed_application: Construct breast/back interfaces, edges and waist transition as assemblies, not a single inflated torso.
sources.limitation: Museum dimensions are not Ada dimensions. Some surviving/replaced hardware is explicitly modern; do not infer all original kinematics.

sources.title: The Met — Breastplate, German or Austrian
sources.kind: Museum collection; Public Domain image reference
sources.reviewed_access: Collection page and front image reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: The image provides a readable example of a broad central shell, arm openings and separately readable lower bands.
sources.proposed_application: Study cross-sectional curvature and restrained form hierarchy before adding decoration.
sources.limitation: Not a female-body fitting blueprint or an exact costume match; use Ada's own approved reference for identity.

sources.title: The Met — Breastplate with Tassets, 2013.28
sources.kind: Museum collection; Public Domain image record
sources.reviewed_access: Collection description reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: The description distinguishes the breastplate, movable gussets, waist plate, skirt and tassets.
sources.proposed_application: Keep hip/waist protection separate from the chest shell so stepping can be designed.
sources.limitation: Do not add all these elements if absent from Ada's approved design.

sources.title: Cleveland Museum — Pauldron (right), 1916.1816.c
sources.reviewed_access: Object text reviewed; extracted page reported image unavailable
sources.source_supported_observation: The record identifies shoulder armor with etched decorative bands and roundels.
sources.proposed_application: A research target for shoulder silhouette and later restrained surface accents.
sources.limitation: No detailed image or motion was obtained here. The gallery links to the object rather than inventing a plate arrangement.

sources.title: Blue Spirit — Fantasy Armor
sources.reviewed_access: Indexed creator description reviewed; viewer/archive NOT inspected
sources.source_supported_observation: The creator lists Blender 3.5, Substance texturing, 15.5k triangles and CC Attribution licensing.
sources.proposed_application: Optional one-model inspection of part organization and material hierarchy.
sources.limitation: License/archive must be checked on acquisition. No claim that the model is rigged, compatible, high quality under motion, or licensed for every intended use.

sources.title: Customizable Armor set with damage — original ArtStation breakdown
sources.reviewed_access: Indexed creator text reviewed; full page/visual breakdown not loaded
sources.source_supported_observation: The author describes staged damage layers, planned UVs and packed masks for Unreal materials.
sources.proposed_application: Defer damage variants; retain intentional UV/material-mask planning after the undamaged silhouette works.
sources.limitation: Do not claim the videos/images were reviewed. This is optional pipeline inspiration, not instructions copied from a paid course.

sources.title: The Met — Open Access image/data policy
sources.reviewed_access: Policy reviewed
sources.source_supported_observation: The Met makes designated public-domain images available under CC0; other images may have restrictions.
sources.proposed_application: Use only individually verified Public Domain/OA images when caching references.
sources.limitation: A museum-wide policy is not blanket clearance for every page image. No third-party media is bundled in this kit.

sources.title: Blender 5.1 — Render Baking
sources.reviewed_access: Documentation reviewed; localized title, relevant technical passages readable
sources.source_supported_observation: Selected-to-active transfers surface detail; tangent-space normals can be used on animated objects.
sources.proposed_application: Bake fine quilting, shallow engraving and edge treatment after geometry and the runtime mesh are stable.
sources.limitation: Normal detail does not change silhouette or solve collision; inspect cage, rays, seams and engine convention.
